How many of these exist in science and m.Fundamental forces: Gravity, electromagnetism and the strong and weak nuclear forces; unifying all four into one theory is physics' biggest unfinished project.
How many of these exist in science and m.Platonic solids: Only five convex shapes have identical regular faces and the same arrangement at every corner; Euclid's Elements ends by proving there are no more.
How many of these exist in science and m.Quark flavours: Up, down, strange, charm, bottom and top; the top quark is roughly as heavy as a whole gold atom, vastly more than the up quark.
How many of these exist in science and m.SI base units: The metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole and candela; since 2019 all are defined by constants of nature, and no physical object defines the kilogram.
How many of these exist in science and m.Archimedean solids: These semi-regular solids mix two or more kinds of regular polygon; a classic football's pattern is the truncated icosahedron, one of the thirteen.
How many of these exist in science and m.Bravais lattices (3D): Auguste Bravais classified crystals in the 1800s; every crystal's repeating atom grid fits one of these 14 patterns, from simple cubic to face-centred.
How many of these exist in science and m.Wallpaper symmetry groups: Every repeating flat design, from Alhambra tilework to wallpaper, falls into one of 17 symmetry types, a result proved in 1891.
How many of these exist in science and m.Standard amino acids: Cells build every protein from 20 standard amino acids; humans cannot make nine of them, so we must get those from food.
How many of these exist in science and m.Named chemical elements: Oganesson, element 118, completed the periodic table's seventh row; it is man-made, and it was officially named in 2016.
How many of these exist in science and m.Crystallographic space groups: In 1891 Fedorov and Schoenflies independently listed all 230 ways atoms can be arranged symmetrically in a 3D crystal.

Tennis greats, by first Grand Slam title.Rod Laver: Rod Laver won the calendar-year Grand Slam twice, in 1962 and 1969, and Melbourne's arena is named for him.
Tennis greats, by first Grand Slam title.Bjorn Borg: Bjorn Borg won six French Open titles, and he retired at 26, famously cool under pressure.
Tennis greats, by first Grand Slam title.Martina Navratilova: Martina Navratilova won Wimbledon nine times, and she defected from Czechoslovakia in 1975 to live in the United States.
Tennis greats, by first Grand Slam title.Steffi Graf: Steffi Graf won the Golden Slam in 1988, taking all four majors and Olympic gold in a single year.
Tennis greats, by first Grand Slam title.Pete Sampras: Pete Sampras won 14 majors and was famed for his big serve, and he took seven Wimbledon titles.
Tennis greats, by first Grand Slam title.Andre Agassi: Andre Agassi won his first major at Wimbledon, and he completed a career Golden Slam by winning the Olympics too.
Tennis greats, by first Grand Slam title.Serena Williams: Serena Williams won her first major at the 1999 US Open, and she went on to win 23 Grand Slam singles titles.
Tennis greats, by first Grand Slam title.Roger Federer: Roger Federer won his first major at Wimbledon in 2003, and went on to win 20 Grand Slam singles titles.
Tennis greats, by first Grand Slam title.Rafael Nadal: Rafael Nadal won a record 14 French Open titles, and he earned the nickname King of Clay.
Tennis greats, by first Grand Slam title.Novak Djokovic: Novak Djokovic won his first major at the 2008 Australian Open, and went on to break records for weeks at number one.

Eggs by weight.Quail egg: The tiny quail egg is a delicacy in many cuisines, and its speckled shell pattern is unique to each bird, like a fingerprint.
Eggs by weight.US Peewee egg: A Peewee egg comes from a young hen just starting to lay, so it is small, with a proportionally big yolk.
Eggs by weight.US Small egg: US Small eggs are the lightest of the standard grades, and a dozen must weigh at least 18 ounces by regulation.
Eggs by weight.US Medium egg: Eggs are graded by the weight per dozen, so a Medium dozen must weigh at least 21 ounces.
Eggs by weight.US Large egg: The Large egg is the standard in most recipes, which is why baking directions tend to specify it.
Eggs by weight.US Extra Large egg: Extra Large eggs weigh at least 27 ounces per dozen, and are more common from older, bigger hens.
Eggs by weight.US Jumbo egg: Jumbo eggs weigh at least 30 ounces per dozen and sometimes contain double yolks, which are rare in smaller sizes.
Eggs by weight.Goose egg: Goose eggs are about three times the size of a chicken egg, and their shells are so thick that a hammer-like tap is needed.
Eggs by weight.Emu egg: An emu egg has a dark green shell, and one egg can equal about ten chicken eggs, which fills a good frying pan.
Eggs by weight.Ostrich egg: The ostrich egg is the largest of any living bird, and its shell is so strong that a person can stand on it.

When these classical styles emerged.Gregorian chant: It is named after Pope Gregory I and is sung in unison with no instruments, which gave medieval monasteries their distinctive sound.
When these classical styles emerged.Ars nova: The name means new art, taken from a French treatise, and the style allowed far more rhythmic freedom than the period before.
When these classical styles emerged.Renaissance polyphony: Palestrina's smooth, interwoven voices became the model for the style, and his music was said to have saved church polyphony.
When these classical styles emerged.Baroque: The name comes from the Portuguese word for an irregularly shaped pearl, and it was originally an insult for ornate, excessive style.
When these classical styles emerged.Classical period: Mozart and Haydn defined this era, and sonata form, with its exposition, development and return, shaped most of its large pieces.
When these classical styles emerged.Romanticism: Composers such as Chopin and Schumann poured emotion and individuality into the music, and the piano became the star instrument of the age.
When these classical styles emerged.Impressionism: Debussy disliked the label, which was borrowed from painters like Monet, and his music uses color and mood rather than strict form.
When these classical styles emerged.Twelve-tone serialism: Arnold Schoenberg's method arranges all twelve notes of the scale in a fixed order before any can repeat, which avoids a home key.
When these classical styles emerged.Musique concrète: In Paris, Pierre Schaeffer made music from recorded everyday sounds such as trains, cutting and looping them on discs and then tape.
When these classical styles emerged.Minimalism: Steve Reich, Philip Glass and Terry Riley built music from repeated patterns that change slowly, so the interest comes from small shifts.

When these countries changed their names.Persia becomes Iran: Reza Shah asked the world to use 'Iran', the name its people had long used, which means 'land of the Aryans'.
When these countries changed their names.Siam becomes Thailand: Thailand means 'land of the free'; the name was briefly dropped after World War II and then restored in 1949.
When these countries changed their names.Gold Coast becomes Ghana: Ghana was the first sub-Saharan colony to become independent, and took the name of a medieval West African empire.
When these countries changed their names.Ceylon becomes Sri Lanka: Sri Lanka means 'resplendent island'; the new name came when the country became a republic.
When these countries changed their names.Dahomey becomes Benin: The name Benin came from the Bight of Benin, not the old Kingdom of Benin, which lay in what is now Nigeria.
When these countries changed their names.Rhodesia becomes Zimbabwe: Zimbabwe comes from Great Zimbabwe, the medieval stone city, and replaced a name honoring Cecil Rhodes.
When these countries changed their names.Upper Volta to Burkina Faso: Leader Thomas Sankara picked a name meaning roughly 'land of upright people', blending Mooré and Dioula words.
When these countries changed their names.Burma becomes Myanmar: The ruling military changed the English name, though many governments and people still use 'Burma'.
When these countries changed their names.Zaire becomes DR Congo: Mobutu had named it Zaire in 1971; the country returned to a Congo name after he was overthrown.
When these countries changed their names.Swaziland becomes Eswatini: King Mswati III announced the change to 'land of the Swazis' on the 50th anniversary of independence.

English Bible translations, by publicati.Wycliffe Bible: Hand-copied from Latin and led by John Wycliffe, it was banned, yet copies survived by the hundreds.
English Bible translations, by publicati.Tyndale New Testament: William Tyndale printed it abroad and smuggled it into England; he was strangled and burned in 1536 for it.
English Bible translations, by publicati.Coverdale Bible: It was the first complete Bible printed in English, with Miles Coverdale as its translator.
English Bible translations, by publicati.Geneva Bible: The Bible Shakespeare and the Pilgrims knew, it popularised verse numbers and study notes in English.
English Bible translations, by publicati.King James Version: King James I commissioned it, and its phrases like 'the skin of my teeth' still shape everyday English.
English Bible translations, by publicati.Revised Version: It was the first major revision of the King James text, aiming to fix errors found in older manuscripts.
English Bible translations, by publicati.Revised Standard Version: It caused a stir by translating Isaiah's 'virgin' as 'young woman'.
English Bible translations, by publicati.New International Version: It became the best-selling modern English translation, aimed at readable everyday English.
English Bible translations, by publicati.New Revised Standard Version: This update to the RSV adopted gender-inclusive language and is widely used in academic study.
English Bible translations, by publicati.English Standard Version: It is a revision of the RSV aimed at being 'essentially literal' in its wording.

Hot temperatures, from hot tub to weldin.Hot tub: Hot tubs are usually limited to about 40 degrees because hotter water risks overheating the body.
Hot temperatures, from hot tub to weldin.Medium steak (center): Medium steak is around 60 degrees inside; surface browning needs far hotter temperatures.
Hot temperatures, from hot tub to weldin.Boiling water: Water boils at 100 only at sea level; at the summit of Everest it boils near 70.
Hot temperatures, from hot tub to weldin.Deep fryer oil: Oil at about 180 drives off moisture as steam, giving fried food its crisp crust.
Hot temperatures, from hot tub to weldin.Wood-fired pizza oven: Neapolitan pizza traditionally bakes in about 60 to 90 seconds in a wood-fired oven.
Hot temperatures, from hot tub to weldin.Aluminium melts: Low for a metal, and recycling it takes about 95 percent less energy than making it new.
Hot temperatures, from hot tub to weldin.Copper melts: Bronze, an alloy of copper and tin, melts lower, which helped make the Bronze Age possible.
Hot temperatures, from hot tub to weldin.Iron melts: Beyond the reach of ancient furnaces, so early smiths hammered iron as a hot solid instead of pouring it.
Hot temperatures, from hot tub to weldin.Oxyacetylene torch: Burning acetylene in pure oxygen gives a flame near 3,200 degrees C, hot enough to cut through thick steel plate.
Hot temperatures, from hot tub to weldin.Electric welding arc: An electric arc reaches roughly the temperature of the Sun's visible surface, around 5,500 degrees C or more.

Phone makers, by founding year.Nokia: Founded in Finland in 1865 as a paper mill, it later made rubber boots and cables before becoming a phone giant. Its name comes from the town of Nokia.
Phone makers, by founding year.Motorola: Started in 1928 as the Galvin Manufacturing Corporation making car radios. The name joins "motor" and "Victrola", and it made the first handheld cellphone call in 1973.
Phone makers, by founding year.Samsung: Its name means "three stars" in Korean. It began in 1938 as a small trading company exporting dried fish, fruit and noodles.
Phone makers, by founding year.Sony: Founded in Tokyo in 1946 by Masaru Ibuka and Akio Morita, it was first called Tokyo Tsushin Kogyo before adopting a name that works worldwide.
Phone makers, by founding year.BlackBerry (RIM): The Canadian company behind the "CrackBerry" craze. Its keyboard-equipped phones were once the favorite of business users and even presidents.
Phone makers, by founding year.Huawei: Founded in Shenzhen in 1987 by Ren Zhengfei, a former army engineer, it began by reselling telephone switches. It now makes networks and phones worldwide.
Phone makers, by founding year.HTC: The Taiwanese company built the first Android phone, the HTC Dream, sold in 2008 as the T-Mobile G1.
Phone makers, by founding year.Oppo: Founded in Guangdong in 2004, this Chinese brand became a top seller in Asia largely through selfie-focused phones and heavy offline retail.
Phone makers, by founding year.Xiaomi: Its name is Chinese for "millet" or "little rice". Founder Lei Jun launched it in 2010 and it grew into one of the world's top phone sellers.
Phone makers, by founding year.OnePlus: The "Never Settle" startup was founded in Shenzhen in 2013 by Pete Lau and Carl Pei. It first sold phones through invitations to build hype.

When the causes of these diseases were f.Cholera traced to water: John Snow mapped deaths around the Broad Street pump in London and had its handle removed.
When the causes of these diseases were f.Anthrax bacterium: Robert Koch's work on it was the first proof that a specific germ causes a specific disease.
When the causes of these diseases were f.Tuberculosis bacterium: Koch announced the bacterium on 24 March, now observed as World TB Day.
When the causes of these diseases were f.First virus (tobacco mosaic): Dmitri Ivanovsky showed that infectious sap passed through filters that stopped bacteria.
When the causes of these diseases were f.Plague bacterium: Alexandre Yersin found it in Hong Kong, and the bacterium Yersinia pestis is named for him.
When the causes of these diseases were f.Malaria via mosquitoes: Ronald Ross traced the parasite through mosquitoes and won the 1902 Nobel Prize.
When the causes of these diseases were f.Yellow fever via mosquitoes: Walter Reed's commission in Cuba showed mosquitoes spread it, with volunteers taking part.
When the causes of these diseases were f.Prions: Stanley Prusiner coined the term, won the 1997 Nobel Prize, and it is linked to mad cow disease.
When the causes of these diseases were f.HIV: Luc Montagnier and Francoise Barre-Sinoussi's team at the Pasteur Institute isolated it, winning a 2008 Nobel.
When the causes of these diseases were f.SARS coronavirus: The cause was pinned down within weeks, a speed unimaginable in Koch's time.

When each animal was first cloned.Frog (Gurdon): John Gurdon moved nuclei from tadpole gut cells into eggs, proving adult cells keep all their genes. He won a Nobel Prize in 2012.
When each animal was first cloned.Sheep (Dolly): Dolly was cloned from a mammary cell and named after Dolly Parton. She lived about six and a half years.
When each animal was first cloned.Pig: Cloned pigs matter for medicine, since pig organs are close to human size and may one day be used for transplants.
When each animal was first cloned.Cat (CC): Her coat pattern differed from her donor's, showing that even clones are not exact copies, since coat patterns arise during development.
When each animal was first cloned.Mule: Idaho Gem was the first cloned equine. Mules are sterile, so cloning is the only way to duplicate one.
When each animal was first cloned.Dog (Snuppy): Created in South Korea, the Afghan hound's name blends Seoul National University and puppy.
When each animal was first cloned.Camel: Born in Dubai, cloned camels were produced to duplicate champion racers, since camel racing is big business there.
When each animal was first cloned.Monkey (Zhong Zhong): The macaque twins Zhong Zhong and Hua Hua were the first primates cloned by the same method as Dolly.
When each animal was first cloned.Przewalski's horse: The foal Kurt came from cells frozen in 1980 at San Diego's Frozen Zoo, restoring lost genes to an endangered wild horse.
When each animal was first cloned.Arctic wolf: Arctic wolves live in Canada's far north and Greenland, and their white coats provide year-round camouflage in snow.

Total lengths of famous bridges.Ponte Vecchio: Shops line this Florence bridge, and it was reportedly the only one in the city spared by retreating German forces in 1944.
Total lengths of famous bridges.Tower Bridge: Often mistaken for London Bridge, it was opened in 1894 and lifts its two roadways for tall ships.
Total lengths of famous bridges.Brooklyn Bridge: In 1884, showman P.T. Barnum marched 21 elephants across it to prove that it was safe.
Total lengths of famous bridges.Millau Viaduct: Its tallest mast stands at about the height of the Eiffel Tower, making it the tallest bridge in the world.
Total lengths of famous bridges.Golden Gate Bridge: Its colour is International Orange, chosen to stand out in the fog and also to complement the surrounding hills.
Total lengths of famous bridges.Øresund Bridge: It runs from Copenhagen to Malmö and dips into a tunnel; it was the setting for the Nordic noir series The Bridge.
Total lengths of famous bridges.Confederation Bridge: It links Prince Edward Island to the mainland and is the longest bridge over ice-covered water in the world.
Total lengths of famous bridges.Lake Pontchartrain Causeway: Its twin spans run so far out that drivers in the middle lose sight of land, especially when fog rolls in.
Total lengths of famous bridges.Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau link: The link includes a long undersea tunnel between artificial islands, opened in 2018 to join three Chinese regions across the Pearl River Delta.
Total lengths of famous bridges.Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge: This viaduct carries a high-speed railway between Beijing and Shanghai and is recognised by Guinness as the world's longest bridge.

Media companies, by founding year.Associated Press: The Associated Press is a not-for-profit news cooperative, founded by New York newspapers to share the costs of telegraph news.
Media companies, by founding year.Reuters: Paul Reuter began by using carrier pigeons to carry stock prices between Aachen and Brussels, before telegraph lines were finished.
Media companies, by founding year.Paramount Pictures: Paramount's logo is said to have been sketched by founder William Hodkinson, based on a mountain from his childhood in Utah.
Media companies, by founding year.BBC: The BBC began as a private company with a few radio programs and became a public corporation in 1927, with its mission to inform, educate and entertain.
Media companies, by founding year.Disney: The Disney Brothers Cartoon Studio was founded by Walt and Roy, and Mickey Mouse arrived five years later.
Media companies, by founding year.HBO: HBO was among the first services to deliver movies by satellite, and it later became known for original shows like The Sopranos.
Media companies, by founding year.CNN: Ted Turner's CNN was the first 24-hour news channel, and its coverage of the Gulf War made it famous.
Media companies, by founding year.Pixar: Pixar began as a computer division of Lucasfilm, and Steve Jobs bought it in 1986 before it made Toy Story.
Media companies, by founding year.DreamWorks: DreamWorks was founded by Steven Spielberg, Jeffrey Katzenberg and David Geffen, and it made Shrek.
Media companies, by founding year.Spotify: Spotify was created in Sweden, and the name reportedly came from a misheard phrase shouted by a founder.

How much energy these store.CR2032 coin cell: It powers key fobs, watches and computer memory backups, and can last for years.
How much energy these store.AA alkaline battery: One AA cell is 14.5 mm wide and 50 mm long, a size standard dating to the early 1900s.
How much energy these store.Smartphone battery: That is only about 13 food calories, and yet it keeps a phone running for a day.
How much energy these store.Laptop battery: Airlines limit spare ones to 100 Wh each in carry-on bags, because of fire risk.
How much energy these store.E-bike battery: Enough to power a bike for dozens of kilometres, depending on how hard you pedal.
How much energy these store.Tesla Powerwall 2: A home battery that stores the sun's power from the day for use at night.
How much energy these store.Original Nissan Leaf: The Leaf was among the first mass-market electric cars, with a range of about 117 km on a charge.
How much energy these store.Gallon of gasoline: That figure is used by US regulators to calculate miles-per-gallon-equivalent ratings for electric vehicles.
How much energy these store.Tesla Model 3 Long Range: The car's long-range version can go over 500 km on a charge.
How much energy these store.GMC Hummer EV: The pack alone is reported to weigh roughly 1,300 kg.

Trickier Roman numerals, by value.XIX: Roman numerals have no zero, and the subtractive IX trick keeps long strings short.
Trickier Roman numerals, by value.XXIX: The numerals began appearing on Super Bowls from Super Bowl V on, which gives fans something to decode.
Trickier Roman numerals, by value.XLIV: Ancient Romans often wrote IIII for four, and many clock faces still use it today.
Trickier Roman numerals, by value.LXXXVIII: At eight characters, this is the longest numeral under 100.
Trickier Roman numerals, by value.XCIX: People often write IC for 99, but the correct form is XCIX, which subtracts the ten from the hundred, then the one from the ten.
Trickier Roman numerals, by value.CXC: The letter C comes from the Latin 'centum', or hundred.
Trickier Roman numerals, by value.CDXLIV: This one holds three subtractive pairs in a row, a neat Roman numeral workout.
Trickier Roman numerals, by value.DCCC: The letter D stands for 500, supposedly half of an old symbol for 1,000.
Trickier Roman numerals, by value.MCMXC: The band Enigma used this as the title of its debut album, MCMXC a.D.
Trickier Roman numerals, by value.MMXXVI: The year of the Milan Cortina Winter Olympics and the FIFA World Cup.

More HTTP status messages, by code.Partial Content: It lets a downloader resume a file or a video stream skip ahead, using the Range header.
More HTTP status messages, by code.Found: The status was originally named Moved Temporarily, and is used for redirects.
More HTTP status messages, by code.Bad Request: The generic response for a request the server can't parse, from broken cookies to malformed URLs.
More HTTP status messages, by code.Unauthorized: Misnamed: it really means unauthenticated, while 403 is permission denied.
More HTTP status messages, by code.Method Not Allowed: The server knows the URL but not the verb, such as POST on a read-only page.
More HTTP status messages, by code.Too Many Requests: Servers use it for rate limiting, often sending a Retry-After header to say when to try again.
More HTTP status messages, by code.Unavailable For Legal Reasons: A nod to Ray Bradbury's novel Fahrenheit 451, for content blocked for legal reasons.
More HTTP status messages, by code.Internal Server Error: A catch-all meaning the server hit something unexpected; the fault is theirs, not yours.
More HTTP status messages, by code.Bad Gateway: A proxy received an invalid response from the server behind it.
More HTTP status messages, by code.Gateway Timeout: A proxy gave up waiting for an upstream server that was too slow.

When these infamous crimes happened.Gunpowder Plot: Guy Fawkes was caught guarding barrels of gunpowder under Parliament, and Britain still burns his effigy every 5 November.
When these infamous crimes happened.Blood's Crown Jewels heist: Colonel Thomas Blood tried to steal the Crown Jewels from the Tower, yet Charles II pardoned him.
When these infamous crimes happened.Jack the Ripper murders: The Whitechapel murders remain unsolved, and the killer's identity is still debated.
When these infamous crimes happened.Mona Lisa stolen: Vincenzo Peruggia, a former Louvre worker, hid the painting under his coat; the theft made the Mona Lisa world-famous.
When these infamous crimes happened.St. Valentine's Day Massacre: Seven men were shot in a Chicago garage, a crime linked to rivals of Al Capone.
When these infamous crimes happened.Lindbergh baby kidnapping: The kidnapping of Charles Lindbergh's baby son led to a federal law against kidnapping across state lines.
When these infamous crimes happened.Great Train Robbery: A gang stole about £2.6 million from a Royal Mail train in Buckinghamshire.
When these infamous crimes happened.D. B. Cooper hijacking: A hijacker, with a bomb threat, extorted $200,000 and parachuted from a Boeing 727; he vanished.
When these infamous crimes happened.Brink's-Mat robbery: Gold bullion worth about £26 million vanished from a warehouse near Heathrow, and some of the metal was reportedly melted into jewellery.
When these infamous crimes happened.Gardner Museum heist: Thieves disguised as police stole 13 artworks, including a Vermeer, and the empty frames still hang in Boston.

Gadgets that changed daily life.Sony Walkman: The Sony Walkman made music portable and personal, and its original name in some markets was Soundabout or Stowaway.
Gadgets that changed daily life.Palm Pilot: The Palm Pilot popularized the handheld organizer and helped pave the way for smartphones, with its Graffiti handwriting system.
Gadgets that changed daily life.TiVo: TiVo pioneered the digital video recorder, and it let people pause live TV and skip ads.
Gadgets that changed daily life.iPod: The iPod put 1,000 songs in your pocket, and it helped launch Apple's turnaround.
Gadgets that changed daily life.Roomba: Roomba is a robotic vacuum from iRobot, a company that had previously built military robots.
Gadgets that changed daily life.Amazon Kindle: The Kindle made e-books mainstream, and its first model sold out in about five and a half hours.
Gadgets that changed daily life.Fitbit Tracker: Fitbit helped popularize wearable step counters, and its first tracker clipped to a belt.
Gadgets that changed daily life.Chromecast: Chromecast is a small dongle that sends video from your phone to the TV, and it cost just 35 dollars at launch.
Gadgets that changed daily life.Amazon Echo: Amazon Echo introduced the Alexa voice assistant to homes, and it was said to be inspired by the computer in Star Trek.
Gadgets that changed daily life.Oculus Quest: Oculus Quest was a standalone VR headset that didn't need a PC or cables.

First editions of these music festivals.Newport Jazz Festival: Newport Jazz Festival started the modern festival, and in 1965 Bob Dylan went electric at its sister Folk Festival.
First editions of these music festivals.Monterey Pop: Monterey Pop showcased Jimi Hendrix and Janis Joplin, and Hendrix set his guitar on fire onstage.
First editions of these music festivals.Woodstock: Woodstock drew about 400,000 people to a dairy farm in upstate New York, and it was meant to be a smaller event.
First editions of these music festivals.Glastonbury: Glastonbury began on a Somerset farm, and in later years it has become the world's most celebrated festival.
First editions of these music festivals.Live Aid: Live Aid was held in London and Philadelphia on the same day to raise money for famine relief in Ethiopia.
First editions of these music festivals.SXSW: SXSW began as a music event in Austin, and later added film and tech, and launched Twitter's breakout.
First editions of these music festivals.Lollapalooza: Lollapalooza was started by Perry Farrell, the Jane's Addiction singer, as a farewell tour for his band.
First editions of these music festivals.Coachella: Coachella takes place in the California desert, and it started after Pearl Jam played the venue in 1993.
First editions of these music festivals.Bonnaroo: Bonnaroo takes place on a farm in Manchester, Tennessee, and its name is from a Dr. John album.
First editions of these music festivals.Tomorrowland: Tomorrowland is an electronic dance festival in Boom, Belgium, and it sells out in minutes.

When these discoveries won the Nobel in.Mosquitoes spread malaria: Ronald Ross showed that mosquitoes carry the malaria parasite. He did it by dissecting insects in India.
When these discoveries won the Nobel in.Pavlov on digestion: Ivan Pavlov won for work on digestion, using dogs. His famous conditioned reflex experiments came out of the same research.
When these discoveries won the Nobel in.Nervous system structure: Camillo Golgi and Santiago Ramón y Cajal shared this prize for their work on nerve cells. They disagreed about how neurons connect.
When these discoveries won the Nobel in.Insulin: Banting and Macleod won for discovering insulin. Banting shared his prize money with his assistant Charles Best.
When these discoveries won the Nobel in.Penicillin: Fleming spotted a mould killing bacteria in 1928. Florey and Chain turned it into a usable drug, sharing the prize.
When these discoveries won the Nobel in.Structure of DNA: Watson, Crick and Wilkins won for the double helix. Rosalind Franklin's X-ray images were critical, but she had died.
When these discoveries won the Nobel in.Split-brain research: Roger Sperry studied patients whose brain hemispheres had been disconnected. He found each half has its own specialities.
When these discoveries won the Nobel in.Prions: Stanley Prusiner discovered these misfolded proteins that cause diseases like mad cow disease. Many scientists first dismissed the idea.
When these discoveries won the Nobel in.IVF: Robert Edwards pioneered in vitro fertilisation. Louise Brown, the first IVF baby, was born in 1978.
When these discoveries won the Nobel in.mRNA vaccines: Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman modified mRNA so it wouldn't trigger immune attack. It enabled COVID-19 vaccines to be developed quickly.

When these modern board games came out.Carcassonne: Klaus-Jürgen Wrede based it on the walled French city, and players build roads, cities and farms by placing tiles.
When these modern board games came out.Puerto Rico: Andreas Seyfarth's game of colonial planting topped BoardGameGeek's ranking for years.
When these modern board games came out.Agricola: Uwe Rosenberg's farming game makes you feed your family every harvest, and it launched a wave of worker-placement games.
When these modern board games came out.Pandemic: Matt Leacock's game has players fight outbreaks together, helping popularize cooperative board games.
When these modern board games came out.7 Wonders: Antoine Bauza's civilization game is played over three ages, with players passing cards around the table to neighbors.
When these modern board games came out.King of Tokyo: Magic: The Gathering creator Richard Garfield made it, and rolling dice decides which monsters brawl over Tokyo.
When these modern board games came out.Splendor: Players collect gem chips to buy cards, and the chunky poker-chip-style tokens are a big part of its charm.
When these modern board games came out.Terraforming Mars: Jacob Fryxelius's game has corporations making Mars habitable, and the cards carry many real science details.
When these modern board games came out.Gloomhaven: Isaac Childres's campaign game topped BoardGameGeek's ranking, and its huge box weighs around 10 kg.
When these modern board games came out.Wingspan: Elizabeth Hargrave designed it as her first game, and each bird card carries real facts about its wingspan.

The world's tiniest countries by area.Vatican City: The world's smallest country can be crossed on foot in minutes, and guarded by the Swiss Guard.
The world's tiniest countries by area.Monaco: It is the world's most densely populated country, and its streets host the Grand Prix.
The world's tiniest countries by area.Nauru: Phosphate from ancient seabird droppings once made it rich, but it has been mined out.
The world's tiniest countries by area.Tuvalu: Its airstrip doubles as a gathering place, and the villagers use the runway as a sports field.
The world's tiniest countries by area.San Marino: It claims to be the world's oldest republic, founded in 301 AD by Saint Marinus.
The world's tiniest countries by area.Liechtenstein: It is one of only two doubly landlocked countries in the world, with Uzbekistan.
The world's tiniest countries by area.Saint Kitts and Nevis: It is the smallest country in the Americas by both area and population.
The world's tiniest countries by area.Malta: Its language, Maltese, is the only Semitic language written in the Latin alphabet in the European Union, a mix of Arabic and Italian.
The world's tiniest countries by area.Andorra: It is ruled by two co-princes: the French president and the Spanish bishop of Urgell.
The world's tiniest countries by area.Singapore: It has grown by roughly a quarter since independence in 1965, through land reclamation.

Egg weights of birds.Bee hummingbird: The smallest bird on Earth, native to Cuba, lays eggs about the size of a coffee bean.
Egg weights of birds.Zebra finch: This Australian songbird breeds readily in captivity, so scientists use it to study how birds learn to sing.
Egg weights of birds.Robin: The beautiful blue of a robin's eggs is so recognized that a shade of blue is named after it.
Egg weights of birds.Japanese quail: Quail eggs are speckled for camouflage, and each female's pattern is distinctive, which helps identify her eggs.
Egg weights of birds.Pigeon: Pigeons produce 'crop milk' to feed their chicks, a cheesy secretion made by both parents.
Egg weights of birds.Chicken: A hen's egg yolk is a single giant cell, and the shell has thousands of tiny pores to let air through.
Egg weights of birds.Duck: Duck eggs have larger yolks and richer flavor than chicken eggs, which is why pastry chefs favor them.
Egg weights of birds.Goose: A goose egg is about three times the volume of a chicken egg, and geese often return to the same nest each year.
Egg weights of birds.Emu: Emu eggs are dark green, and in this species the male alone sits on the eggs for about eight weeks without eating.
Egg weights of birds.Ostrich: The largest egg of any living bird is about 15 centimeters long, and its shell is strong enough to bear a person's weight.

Indian rivers, by length.Sabarmati: Gandhi founded his ashram on its banks in Ahmedabad, and the city has since reshaped the riverfront into a public promenade.
Indian rivers, by length.Luni: Flowing through the Thar Desert region of Rajasthan, this river is salty in its lower reaches, and its name means 'salt river'.
Indian rivers, by length.Tapti: Flowing west across central India to the Arabian Sea, this river passes through Surat, a major diamond-cutting center.
Indian rivers, by length.Kaveri: Often called the 'Ganges of the South', it's revered across Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, and shared water has caused long disputes.
Indian rivers, by length.Mahanadi: Its name means 'great river', and the Hirakud Dam on it is among the longest earthen dams in the world.
Indian rivers, by length.Narmada: Pilgrims walk the whole river's length in a circumambulation called the Narmada Parikrama, and its dams have been highly controversial.
Indian rivers, by length.Krishna: It flows from the Western Ghats to the Bay of Bengal, and ancient cities like Amaravati grew along its banks.
Indian rivers, by length.Godavari: Often called the 'Dakshin Ganga', this is peninsular India's longest river, and the Kumbh-like Pushkaram festival takes place on its banks.
Indian rivers, by length.Ganges: Considered sacred in Hinduism, it is known as the goddess Ganga, and the river basin supports hundreds of millions of people.
Indian rivers, by length.Indus: This river gave India its name and nurtured one of the world's earliest civilizations, though most of its length now lies in Pakistan.
